decisions.reason: Changing the webhook query's contract-address filter does not alter the approved migration data-retention policy or deployment strategy.
The requirement already refers abstractly to the active replacement contract; the webhook filter configuration does not change its ownership or mint-reporting rules.
The platform-statistics scope remains activity from the active replacement contract, and the source does not change any statistics or prize-pool reporting rule.
Applying a contract filter to the webhook query does not necessarily change referral, commission, ticket, or leaderboard accounting requirements.

Although the Discord history mentions a future production-webhook system-log channel, the source only configures the separate contract-event query and does not require any Discord server-state change.
The contract address in the webhook filter is unrelated to remediation of the production-domain malicious-site warning.
The book-access requirement already targets NFTs from the active replacement contract, and the source does not change Lit Protocol ownership checks or access eligibility.
The webhook's smart-contract address filter has no effect on the help form's placement, fields, purposes, or submission behavior.
The source changes an infrastructure query filter and does not modify any About-page content or copy.
The webhook filter configuration does not alter any approved FAQ topic, reward amount, or explanatory copy.
Changing the contract-event query filter does not alter the token-serial referral-code source, persistence, or display locations.
The source does not change prize payout mode, claim-control visibility, or any other prize-claim behavior.
